questions.prompt: Name a bone or named group of bones in the human skeleton.
questions.scope: Standard named bones, fused bones and familiar bone groups count. Left and right instances are the same answer. Cartilage, joints, muscles and organs are not bones.
questions.rationale: A concrete familiar entry point and a wider factual tail, following the saved review; this asks for a different activity or object relationship rather than a tag combination.

questions.prompt: Name a unit used to measure a physical quantity or digital information.
questions.scope: Established metric, customary, historical and scientific measurement units count, including named prefixed units. Currency units and arbitrary made-up units do not. Official unit symbols are accepted only when they name that actual unit.
questions.rationale: A concrete familiar entry point and a wider factual tail, following the saved review; this asks for a different activity or object relationship rather than a tag combination.

questions.prompt: Name a structure or component found in a living cell.
questions.scope: Plant, animal, fungal and prokaryotic cell structures count. Whole organs or tissues are not structures inside one cell. Established molecular structures such as DNA and chromosomes count. Cellular structures and molecular assemblies count; an individual pigment such as chlorophyll is not an organelle or cell structure by itself.
questions.rationale: A concrete familiar entry point and a wider factual tail, following the saved review; this asks for a different activity or object relationship rather than a tag combination.

note: Complete prefix names and the named SI units are factual NIST terminology. Mass prefixes attach to gram, not kilogram. No automatically constructed initialisms or prefixed unit symbols are emitted because symbol case matters.
